function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a convenient delivery service.

---

## 1️⃣ Local Bakeries & Specialty Shops  
These places often offer fresh, made‑to‑order cakes and can accommodate custom designs.

| Type | What to Look For | How to Order |
|------|------------------|--------------|
| **Independent Bakery** | Freshly baked, seasonal ingredients, local reputation | Call or visit their website; many accept phone orders or have an online form |
| **Cake Boutique** | Custom décor, themed cakes, premium frosting | Email or use their online “Custom Order” page; some allow live chat |
| **Gourmet Dessert Shop** | Artisan flavors, vegan/gluten‑free options | Check their menu online; place orders via email or phone |

### Tips
- **Check Reviews** – Google Maps, Yelp, or Instagram comments can give you a sense of quality and reliability.
- **Ask About Delivery** – Some local shops deliver within a certain radius; others may only pick up.
- **Confirm Cut‑Off Times** – Most bakeries require orders at least 24–48 hrs in advance for custom cakes.

---

## 2️⃣ Online Delivery Platforms  
If you want convenience and a wide selection, these apps let you browse multiple vendors from one place.

| Platform | Strengths | Typical Vendors |
|----------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Uber Eats** | Fast delivery, real‑time tracking | Local bakeries, chain restaurants, specialty dessert shops |
| **DoorDash** | Wide coverage, frequent promos | Independent bakeries, national chains, artisanal shops |
| **Postmates** | Same‑day delivery, flexible pickup | Local cafés, boutique bakeries, food trucks |
| **Instacart** | Grocery + bakery items | Supermarkets, local grocery stores, specialty markets |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Large inventory, Prime benefits | Supermarket chains, local produce markets |

### How to Use
1. **Search “cake” or “birthday cake”** in your city.  
2. Filter by **delivery time**, **price**, or **customer rating**.  
3. Read vendor profiles for photos, flavor options, and delivery policies.  
4. Place your order through the app; most platforms support contactless delivery.

---

## 3️⃣ National Chains & Online Retailers  
Great for standardized cakes, large parties, or when you need a quick solution.

| Vendor | What They Offer | Ordering Method |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Panera Bread** | Freshly baked cupcakes, simple birthday cakes | Phone or website |
| **Dunkin’ Donuts** | Birthday cakes, custom messages | Phone or mobile app |
| **Baker’s Dozen** | Custom cakes, vegan options | Website or phone |
| **Amazon** | Pre‑made cakes, gift boxes | Amazon.com (Prime delivery) |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, artisanal cakes from independent sellers | Etsy.com (direct seller communication) |

### Tips
- **Look for “Made‑to‑Order”** – Even chain stores often have a “custom” option.  
- **Check Delivery Fees** – Some chains charge extra for delivery beyond a certain distance.  
- **Read Return Policies** – Especially for online retailers; some offer refunds if the cake arrives damaged.

---

## 4️⃣ Specialty Services & Subscription Boxes  
If you’re into unique flavors or want a recurring treat.

| Service | Highlights | How to Subscribe |
|---------|-------------|------------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Gourmet cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S. | Browse catalog → add to cart → checkout |
| **The Cake Club** | Monthly cake subscription (variety of flavors) | Sign up on their website → choose plan |
| **Dessert Delivery** | Vegan, gluten‑free, keto options | Search by dietary preference → place order |

---

## Quick Checklist Before You Order

1. **Flavor & Size** – Confirm what you want and how many servings it covers.  
2. **Delivery Time** – Make sure the vendor can meet your deadline.  
3. **Special Requests** – Communicate any allergies, dietary restrictions, or design ideas early.  
4. **Payment Options** – Check if they accept credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, etc.  
5. **Contactless Delivery** – If you prefer no‑contact drop‑off, confirm this option is available.

---

### Final Thought  
If you’re ordering for a special occasion, consider placing your order at least 48 hours in advance to ensure freshness and availability. And don’t forget to tip your delivery driver if you’re using a third‑party platform—most people appreciate a little extra for their hard work!

Happy cake hunting! 🍰
